page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system provides 16.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistent data.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core metrics placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling within the middle 50% average. A notable performance limitation is observed in multi-threaded decompression, where bzip3 decompression results are weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only large block speeds at 68.67 GB/sec and write speeds at 49.73 GB/sec.

With its compute-focused allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for CPU-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints or local NVMe storage. It is suitable for tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference, as demonstrated by its average performance in Clang compilation and small-model LLM text generation.
